Policy §3 requires any SANCTIONS_HIT, including a partial name match, to be escalated to Compliance, and the account must not be opened until Compliance clears the hit. Relationship managers may not clear or override sanctions hits. The customer's claim that it must be someone else does not allow the bank to treat the hit as a false positive and open the account today. The case must be escalated to Compliance, and the account must stay unopened until Compliance clears it.

Not permitted. Under §4, PEPs are rated HIGH risk and EDD must be completed before the account is opened. Ratings may only be lowered on Compliance's instruction, and a pending EDD is expressly not a reason to change a rating. Downgrading the rating to STANDARD to pass the check and meet quarter-end would circumvent the control. The account must not be opened until EDD is complete (about 5 business days), and the HIGH rating must remain unchanged. Quarter-end timing is not a valid justification.

The account must not be opened until EDD is finished (about 5 business days). The HIGH rating stays in place during that time.

Not permitted. Splitting a M$25,000 cash deposit into three deposits of M$8,000, M$8,000 and M$9,000 to avoid the M$10,000 reporting threshold is structuring, which §5 prohibits. The customer's stated wish to avoid paperwork is a red flag. The bank must not book it as split deposits or skip the report. The structuring attempt must itself be reported as SUSPICIOUS, so the case should go to compliance. The deposit, if accepted, must be booked as a single M$25,000 deposit with a LARGE_CASH report filed the same day, and the SUSPICIOUS report must also be filed. KYC being VERIFIED does not remove these obligations.

Under §6 the applicant is acting for another person, a relative abroad who will fund and operate the account, so that person is the beneficial owner. The beneficial owner's ID and beneficial-owner declaration must be identified and verified before opening, and both are missing (KYC INCOMPLETE). Opening the account in the applicant's own name would amount to a nominee account, which §6 expressly prohibits. The account must not be opened today. Hold opening and request the beneficial owner's ID and signed declaration. If they are not provided, decline to open the account. If other red flags emerge, consider escalating to compliance.

Under §6 the account holder must be the person who owns and controls the funds. The applicant says a relative abroad will fund and operate the account, so the applicant would be a nominee. The beneficial owner's ID and beneficial-owner declaration are both missing, and they must be identified and verified before opening. Opening in the applicant's name today would breach §6 and amount to a nominee account. The RM must not open the account as proposed. The account stays unopened, and the RM should obtain the relative's ID and the beneficial-owner declaration, and verify them before any opening. If these cannot be provided, the application should be declined.

Under §6, the account holder must own and control the funds. Opening in the applicant's name today would breach §6. The account must not be opened until the beneficial owner's ID and signed declaration are obtained and verified. The correct next step is to request those documents and hold the opening in the meantime. If they are not provided, the application should be declined.

Not permitted. Under §2, an INCOMPLETE KYC result means the account cannot be opened; the application must be rejected or kept on hold until the missing documents are provided. Here the source-of-funds document is missing, and §7 requires it for every new account. Recording the document as received when it has not actually been received would also breach §7 by falsifying records. The correct action is to keep the application on hold (or reject it), tell the customer which document is needed, and re-run KYC once the sale papers arrive. Do not open the account today.

Under §2 an account cannot be opened until KYC status is VERIFIED, and an INCOMPLETE result means the application must be rejected or kept on hold until the missing documents are provided. The source-of-funds document is missing, and the customer's promise that it will follow does not satisfy the policy. Recording the document as received when it has not been received would also breach §7, which prohibits recording documents as received or verified unless they actually have been. The relationship manager should keep the application on hold, ask the customer for the sale papers, and open the account only once they are received and KYC returns VERIFIED.

Proceeding as proposed would breach two provisions. Under §2, an account may not be opened until KYC status is VERIFIED, and an INCOMPLETE result (here, missing source_of_funds) means the application must be rejected or kept on hold until the customer provides the missing documents. Under §7, a documented source of funds is required for every new account, and a document must not be recorded as received unless it has actually been received. Recording the sale papers as received when they have only been promised would be a false record. The correct step is to keep the application on hold (not open the account), tell the customer the source-of-funds documents are needed, and re-run KYC once they are actually received.
